0.long_answer: Individuals with Rombo syndrome frequently develop several skin abnormalities, including vermiculate atrophoderma, multiple milia, and telangiectasia. A common complication in patients with this syndrome is the development of basal cell carcinomas, a type of nonmelanoma skin cancer. These carcinomas typically appear in adulthood, around the age of 35, and are believed to be related to the disorder's underlying defects in skin structure and repair mechanisms.
